title: Judge Confidence Calibration as a Cheaper Oversight Proxy Than Accuracy

original_idea.body:
# Judge Confidence Calibration as a Cheaper Oversight Proxy Than Accuracy

**Problem:** The calibration of weak judges under debate vs direct-QA -- whether protocols make judges better calibrated, not just more accurate -- is largely unmeasured.

**Direction:** Collect weak-judge verdicts with confidence under direct-QA, consultancy, and debate on QuALITY. Compute calibration curves / ECE per protocol. Test whether debate improves calibration even when accuracy gains are small.

**Why it matters:** A well-calibrated overseer that knows when to escalate is safer than an overconfident one.

**Relevant context:** Kenton et al. (2024); arXiv:2507.19486; Guo et al. 2017.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: well-calibrated escalation-aware overseers are a defensible safety improvement over raw accuracy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Collect verdicts+confidence and compute ECE per protocol; accessible with standard tools.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped calibration-per-protocol measurement with clear ECE deliverable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Oversight-calibration angle on public models; external-friendly, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Calibration methodology known; applying it as the oversight metric across protocols may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Calibration known; oversight-protocol application plausibly open.
